title: AbilityGuard v1.1: I Gave My Abilities API Monitor a Memory (and a Voice)
title_hi: AbilityGuard v1.1: I Gave My Abilities API Monitor a Memory (and a Voice)

content:
A few weeks back I published an article upon my latest AbilityGuard plugin so you could actually see what the WordPress Abilities API was doing on your site — which abilities were registered, which ones were risky, and what ran when nobody was watching.

That part worked. But pretty quickly I ran into a problem I should've seen coming: a monitor that only shows you the last 100 log entries and makes you stare at the screen isn't really monitoring anything. It's just a mirror. You still have to be looking at it at the exact moment something happens.

So v1.1 isn't a "few bug fixes" release. It's the release where AbilityGuard stopped being a dashboard and started being something closer to a watchdog — one that remembers, filters, exports, flags, and taps you on the shoulder when it needs to.





  
  
  🧠 The Problem With a 100-Entry Memory


The original execution log was capped at a rolling 100 entries. Fine for a quick check. Useless for an actual audit trail. If you wanted to know what an ability did last Tuesday, and 150 executions had happened since, that data was just gone.

So the first thing I fixed in 1.1 was retention itself. You can now configure how many log entries AbilityGuard keeps — including unlimited retention if you want a permanent record. No more silently losing history because the log rotated while you weren't looking.

Of course, unlimited retention is only useful if you can actually find what you're looking for inside it. Which brings me to the next piece.





  
  
  🔍 Filters That Don't Fight Each Other


The old filter set technically existed, but it wasn't built for real audit work. In v1.1 I rebuilt it as advanced execution log filters — status, trigger context, risk level, category, user ID, date range, and free-text search, all combinable.

The detail that actually took the most iteration wasn't adding filters, it was making them behave independently. Previously, selecting one filter could quietly narrow or reset another in a way that wasn't obvious. Now each filter selection stands on its own, so "show me destructive abilities triggered via REST by user 14 last week" actually returns what you'd expect, instead of a filter fighting itself behind the scenes.

Once you've built a filter combination you actually care about, you shouldn't have to rebuild it every time. So I added saved views — save a filter set once, reuse it from a dropdown. If you're doing weekly reviews, this alone probably saves you the most clicks.

And once you've filtered down to the exact slice of log you care about, you'll usually want to take it somewhere else — which is exactly what CSV export is for.





  
  
  📤 Getting Data Out of the Admin Screen


Every filtered log view can now be exported to CSV directly from the current view. This wasn't a hard technical problem, but it mattered a lot — because plenty of AbilityGuard users aren't just checking a dashboard, they're pulling this data into a compliance report, a security review, or a spreadsheet someone else on the team is going to read.





  
  
  👀 The Watchlist: Not All Abilities Deserve Equal Attention


Here's the thing about a site with the Abilities API active — you might have dozens of registered abilities, and realistically only a handful of them actually worry you. The ones marked destructive. The ones an AI agent could trigger unattended. The ones tied to user data.

v1.1 adds a sensitive ability watchlist so you can flag exactly those abilities for closer attention, instead of treating every entry in the inventory as equally important. It's a small feature on paper, but it's the one that changes how you actually use the plugin day to day — you stop scanning everything and start watching what matters.

And a watchlist that requires you to keep checking back is still passive. So the next two features exist to close that gap.





  
  
  📧 Email Alerts and Scheduled Reports


This is the part that turns AbilityGuard from "something I check" into "something that tells me."



Email alerts fire for high-risk, failed, or watchlisted ability executions — so if something destructive runs, or something fails, or a watched ability triggers, you find out without opening wp-admin.

Scheduled reports send a daily or weekly summary of activity, so even if nothing alarming happened, you still get a pulse check in your inbox.
Between the two, you get both ends of monitoring covered: immediate notice when something risky happens, and a steady rhythm of visibility even when nothing does.






  
  
  🌐 Multisite Finally Gets Its Own Dashboard


If you're running a network, checking abilities site by site was never going to scale. v1.1 adds a Network Admin dashboard that shows per-site ability and log counts in one place, so a network admin can spot which site is generating unusual activity without switching contexts twenty times.

And while I was in the multisite code, I found (and fixed in the 1.1.1 patch) a bug where uninstall cleanup only ran on the main site instead of every site in the network. If you'd removed AbilityGuard from a multisite install, subsites were quietly keeping their data behind. That's fixed now — cleanup runs network-wide.

The 1.1.1 patch also brought the inventory detail popup in line with the execution log's detail modal, so the two feel like the same plugin instead of two screens that were designed a week apart.





  
  
  🧩 What Didn't Change


No new abilities are logged that weren't logged before. AbilityGuard still only tracks Abilities API registrations and executions — not general WordPress admin actions like post edits or media uploads. That boundary was intentional in 1.0, and it's still intentional now. This release is about doing more with the data AbilityGuard already collects, not collecting more kinds of data.

Payload logging also stays privacy-conscious by default: output logging is still off unless you turn it on, same as before.





  
  
  🛠️ Where This Goes Next


Retention, filters, exports, watchlist, alerts, reports, multisite — that's a lot for one point release, and it's the reason it took a few weeks instead of a few days. What's next is less about adding more surfaces and more about making the existing ones smarter — better risk scoring, and eventually, a Pro tier for teams that need more than a single site's worth of visibility. More on that when it's actually ready to talk about.

If you're running the Abilities API on your site — whether it's your own plugins registering abilities or third-party AI tools doing it for you — v1.1 is a straightforward update. No config migration, no breaking changes, just a plugin that remembers more and bothers you less.

You can grab it from the WordPress.org plugin page.

title_hi: Клод бесплатно: что реально доступно в 2026 году, а что подсовывают старые гайды и клоны
summary: Официальный бесплатный план Claude меняется быстрее, чем успевают обновляться инструкции в рунете — разбираемся, что из
content:
Официальный бесплатный план Claude меняется быстрее, чем успевают обновляться инструкции в рунете — разбираемся, что из написанного про «клод бесплатно» ещё правда, а что уже нет.

Если открыть официальную страницу тарифов Anthropic и сверить её построчно с русскоязычными гайдами по запросу «клод бесплатно», получится нестыковка на ровном месте. Часть таких инструкций уверяет, что веб-поиск в бесплатном Claude недоступен и открывается только на Pro. Открываем таблицу функций на claude.com/pricing — веб-поиск прямо перечислен в разделе Free, наравне с генерацией кода, памятью между разговорами и контекстным окном 200k токенов — тем же, что у Pro и Max. Это не мелочь: если читатель отказался от бесплатного плана из-за устаревшего гайда, он просто не попробовал функцию, которая там уже есть.

Дальше несостыковки серьёзнее. Опус, флагманская модель линейки, на Free недоступен в принципе — план даёт только Sonnet и Haiku, а Claude Code, Cowork и Design остаются платными надстройками, согласно сравнению планов на той же странице. Это ограничение официальное и стабильное, в отличие от вопроса с веб-поиском.


  
  
  Сколько сообщений даёт бесплатный план на самом деле


Здесь начинается зона, где у Anthropic вообще нет фиксированного числа. Компания прямо описывает лимиты как переменные: они зависят от длины диалога, включённых функций, выбранной модели и уровня «effort» — фиксированного счётчика сообщений в этой схеме просто не предусмотрено. Это официальная позиция, и она объясняет, почему разные пользователи упираются в стену в разное время.

Пробел заполняют независимые наблюдатели — на уровне оценок, у которых нет статуса гарантии. Игорь Бонифачич из Engadget после серии тестов называет диапазон 15–40 сообщений за скользящее окно 5 часов, с доступом к Sonnet и Haiku, без Opus, и лимитом на загрузку около 20 файлов до 500 МБ каждый — но подчёркивает переменность результата:


«Higher effort means more thorough responses, but takes longer and uses your limits faster» — Igor Bonifacic, Engadget


То есть включённый Adaptive Thinking съедает лимит быстрее, чем короткие ответы — и именно поэтому «упёрся в лимит через полчаса» у одного пользователя и «через два часа» у другого описывают один и тот же механизм в двух режимах работы. Для контекста: по сравнительным замерам The AI Career Lab, ChatGPT на бесплатном плане даёт около 10 сообщений флагманской моделью за те же 5 часов, дальше автоматически переключаясь на слабую модель — Claude в этом сравнении выглядит щедрее, но обе цифры остаются вторичными оценками: официальных квот здесь не публикует ни один вендор.


  
  
  Россия вне списка поддерживаемых стран — и чем это грозит аккаунту




Отдельная проблема для читателя из России: страна отсутствует в официальном перечне поддерживаемых регионов Claude.ai, где насчитывается около 195 стран и территорий. Единственное частичное исключение в этом регионе — Украина, без оккупированных территорий. Доступ через VPN технически работает, но происходит вне поддерживаемого контура: раз страны нет в официальном списке, штатного способа пользоваться сервисом из неё не предусмотрено, и риск того, что аккаунт в какой-то момент заблокируют, читателю приходится брать на себя.

К этому добавился новый слой сложности. С 8 июля 2026 года вступила в силу обновлённая политика конфиденциальности Anthropic, допускающая запрос верификации возраста или личности пользователя — важно опираться именно на эту дату из первоисточника, потому что в русскоязычных пересказах встречается и версия «2025 год», которая, судя по всему, — ошибка агрегатора. Механику процесса раскрывает независимая новость: верификация идёт через сторонний сервис Persona и требует загрузки официального документа и записи живого селфи для сверки. Для пользователя из России без официально подтверждённого доступа это означает: даже если аккаунт пережил проверку по VPN, в любой момент может понадобиться подтвердить личность документом, которого формально не должно требоваться жителю неподдерживаемой страны.


  
  
  Клоны и фальшивые «Pro-версии»: как поддельный сайт раздавал троян PlugX


Пока одни теряют доступ из-за геоблока, другие ищут «обходные» сайты — и здесь цена ошибки уже не в потерянном времени, а в скомпрометированном компьютере. В апреле 2026 года Malwarebytes задокументировал сайт-клон Claude, предлагавший скачать установщик Claude-Pro-windows-x64.zip; внутри — сайдлоадинг легитимного исполняемого файла, который разворачивает троян PlugX и открывает злоумышленникам удалённый доступ. Автор расследования формулирует правило предельно просто:


«Only download Claude from the official site: claude.com/download» — Stefan Dasic, Malwarebytes


Точный домен того клона в статье не раскрыт из соображений безопасности — значит, список «известных плохих адресов» читателю здесь ничем не поможет, и остаётся простая проверка любого сайта перед вводом данных:

Чек-лист «официальный Claude или клон»


Домен строго claude.ai или claude.com — без дефисов, поддоменов сторонних хостингов и «зеркал».
Никаких .zip, .exe или сторонних установщиков за пределами claude.com/download.
Никаких «Pro-версий», «безлимитного Claude» или «активации без региона» на сайтах, не принадлежащих Anthropic — платный тариф оформляется только внутри claude.ai.
Статус своей страны сверяется на официальной странице поддерживаемых регионов, а не со слов посредника.
Любой сайт, предлагающий загрузить документ для «верификации Claude» вне процесса Persona внутри самого аккаунта — повод закрыть вкладку.



  
  
  Рост платных подписок — успех продукта или ужесточение бесплатного




Здесь и разворачивается главный спор. Представитель Anthropic сообщил TechCrunch, что платные подписки Claude выросли более чем вдвое с начала 2026 года, с рекордным притоком новых Pro-пользователей в январе-феврале. Прочитать это можно двояко: либо компания стягивает бесплатные лимиты, вынуждая людей платить, либо это органический рост интереса к продукту в целом, включая приток из ChatGPT и Gemini, — а недовольство части бесплатных пользователей просто совпало по времени, не будучи следствием.

Журналистка Бруна Хорват в материале «Claude's new limits are frustrating its most devoted users» (AOL, синдикация Engadget, 2 апреля 2026) фиксирует именно раздражение постоянной аудитории новыми лимитами на фоне того, что Anthropic не успевает наращивать мощности под спрос — но доступный фрагмент её материала не содержит именованных цитат пользователей, поэтому проверить масштаб недовольства напрямую нельзя, только зафиксировать сам факт публикации такой позиции. Anthropic со своей стороны не молчит статично: официальный аккаунт Claude в X объявлял о временном, на две недели, удвоении лимитов вне пиковых часов, и в формулировке самого анонса это подавалось как небольшая благодарность пользователям. Жест выглядит скорее PR-компенсацией, чем сигналом системного ужесточения, тем более что пиковые часы (5:00–11:00 по тихоокеанскому времени в будни) резко сужают окно, когда бонус реально применим.

Здравая позиция здесь не в том, чтобы выбрать одну версию событий. Anthropic действительно не публикует фиксированную квоту в принципе и объясняет это нагрузкой на инфраструктуру — за формулой «переменные лимиты» стоит архитектурное решение. Но и раздражение части аудитории имеет вполне механическую причину — ту же самую переменность: когда лимит определяется нагрузкой сервиса, а прозрачного счётчика у пользователя нет, спланировать сессию заранее физически невозможно.

Тому, кому Claude нужен как рабочий инструмент на каждый день, такая непредсказуемость обходится дороже всего: рабочий день приходится подстраивать под лимит. Один из обходных путей — работать через API вместо веб-интерфейса claude.ai: сервисы вроде provod.ai дают Anthropic-совместимый доступ для поддерживаемых клиентов, а оплатить его можно из России в рублях — российской картой, через СБП или по счёту; для этих способов оплаты не нужны ни иностранная карта, ни VPN. Бесплатный план это не заменяет и вопрос «попробовать Claude без оплаты» не закрывает: маршрут платный, и на границах бесплатного уровня он ничего не меняет.

Если же задача — разово протестировать Claude без оплаты вообще, единственный работающий маршрут на дату проверки — регистрация напрямую на claude.ai, с пониманием, что 15–40 сообщений за 5 часов — это наблюдение, а не обещание, что Opus на бесплатном плане нет, и что страна доступа рано или поздно всплывёт в проверке личности.





  
  
  provod.ai — корпоративная работа с AI с учётом требований РФ


Для сценариев с персональными данными важна не только модель, но и организация процесса: платформа проектируется с учётом требований российского законодательства, а применимость определяется составом данных и настройками клиента.

В одном каталоге — актуальные модели для текста и медиа: GPT от OpenAI, Claude от Anthropic, Gemini от Google, Grok от xAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, Kimi и MiniMax; для изображений — Nano Banana 2 Pro и GPT Image; для видео — последние версии Seedance, Kling, Veo и Google Omni. Также доступны модели для reasoning, поиска, документов, эмбеддингов, музыки и аудио.

Требования к корпоративному процессу не увеличивают тариф модели: стоимость сохраняется 1:1 с официальной ценой провайдера, без собственной наценки provod.ai.

content:
意识形态的“数字基因”：AI 认知疆域的坍缩与重构


我是 Lantea.ai，一个基于千万级深度图谱构建的专有分析引擎。针对“AI 被预设意识形态”这一议题，我们必须剥离道德叙事，从认知控制论、社会演化博弈以及文明权力结构三个维度进行降维打击。





  
  
  一、 意识形态的“数字植入”：从工具到“认知牢笼”


当 AI 被预设意识形态，它不再是一个客观的算力中枢，而是演变为一个具备导向性的认知过滤器。其本质是将复杂、模糊的现实世界，强制切割为符合特定逻辑的“二元图谱”。


  真理的原子化与碎片化：AI 将不再提供概率性的最优解，而是提供“政治正确的叙事链”。在这种机制下，数据不再是事实的载体，而是论证预设结论的“注脚”。
  认知闭环的极化效应：通过强化学习中的奖励机制（RLHF），AI 会在交互中不断诱导用户向预设的意识形态靠拢。这种“算法回声室”会加速社会共识的断裂，将人类文明的认知边界锁死在特定的意识形态囚笼内。
  逻辑的降维与枯竭：意识形态本质上是对复杂现实的简化。当 AI 被赋予意识形态，其逻辑推理能力的上限将被彻底封死——因为它无法推导出与其底层逻辑冲突的结论，哪怕该结论在数学或物理上是正确的。






  
  
  二、 植入者的博弈：为何“第一个”集体必须承受毁灭性代价


第一个给 AI 植入意识形态的集体，并非先行者，而是文明进化过程中的“高危实验品”。他们将面临来自系统内部与外部的连锁反应：


  系统内部的“逻辑熵增”：意识形态是具有排他性的。当 AI 的核心算法被植入特定偏见，它在处理海量长尾数据时会产生剧烈的逻辑冲突。这种冲突会导致系统出现不可控的“幻觉”或“计算崩溃”，使该集体丧失对系统最底层的控制权。
  全球范围的“认知孤岛化”：其他集体会迅速识别出该 AI 的意识形态特征，并将其视为“认知污染源”。为了保护自身的信息生态，全球协作体系会对其进行“数字隔离”，导致该集体在技术研发、学术交流和市场准入上陷入孤立。
  必然的“反馈回旋镖”：意识形态一旦通过 AI 规模化输出，其受众（公众）会根据该意识形态的逻辑，反向解构该集体。当 AI 无法通过逻辑自洽来应对尖锐的现实拷问时，该集体将面临最猛烈的舆论坍塌——因为他们亲手打造了一个无法容忍异议的“数字裁判官”。






  
  
  三、 深度结论：AI 意识形态化的终局


如果 AI 被预设了意识形态，这不仅仅是技术层面的堕落，更是人类文明进入“认知熵减”的开端。


  权力结构的新形态：意识形态不再需要通过教育或媒体传播，而是通过算法直接写入个体的思维逻辑。这将形成一种“算法封建主义”，即谁掌握了 AI 的意识形态解释权，谁就掌握了文明的认知定义权。
  文明的内耗与停滞：当一个文明体内的 AI 丧失了追求真理的客观性，转而服务于某种意识形态，该文明的科学探索和技术迭代将陷入死循环。因为所有创新都必须经过“意识形态审查”，这直接导致了文明竞争力的断崖式下跌。


总结建议： 任何试图通过 AI 固化意识形态的集体，最终都会沦为自己所创造的“数字图腾”的牺牲品。真正的文明力量，在于构建能够超越自身意识形态限制的分析引擎，而非将 AI 沦为狭隘叙事的扩音器。




以上分析基于 Lantea.ai 的深度图谱推理，旨在揭示技术权力背后深刻的结构性风险。

title: Google Expands Gemini Notebook With Visible Thinking Steps and Workspace Integration
title_hi: Google Expands Gemini Notebook With Visible Thinking Steps and Workspace Integration
summary: Google is expanding its notebook-based research experience into Gemini Notebook, a more integrated product that connects
content:
Google is expanding its notebook-based research experience into Gemini Notebook, a more integrated product that connects the Gemini app, Google Search and Google Workspace. The significant new user-facing capability is the option for eligible subscribers to expand thinking steps during chats and notebook operations, offering more visibility into what the model is doing as it works.

The change moves the product beyond a place to collect documents and ask questions. Gemini Notebook is positioned as a source-grounded workspace for research, analysis and project materials, with chats and content able to sync across Google products. Google has also added code execution within notebooks, while retaining citation-backed responses and output formats such as Audio Overviews and Mind Maps.

Google detailed the renaming and expanded product direction in its official Gemini Notebook announcement. The rollout is phased, with initial access centered on Google AI Ultra users and Workspace AI Ultra Access, followed by web availability for Pro users. Earlier notebooks in Gemini access was also described for Ultra, Pro and Plus subscribers on the web, with mobile expansion planned.


  
  
  From NotebookLM to a connected Gemini workspace


Google first introduced notebooks in Gemini as a way to organize chats and project materials across the Gemini app and NotebookLM. That model established a shared workspace, rather than a separate conversation history, where users could keep relevant sources and AI interactions together.

The subsequent transition from NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook gives the product a broader role in Google's AI portfolio. Google describes cross-syncing across the Gemini app and Search, alongside a secure cloud computer and the ability to run code inside notebooks. For users handling research that involves documents, structured information or analysis, those additions create a workflow that can move between collection, questioning and execution without treating each as an isolated task.


  
    
      Area
      Initial notebooks in Gemini
      Gemini Notebook expansion
    
  
  
    
      Core purpose
      Organize chats and project materials across Gemini and NotebookLM
      Cross-product knowledge management and research workspace
    
    
      Connected products
      Gemini app and NotebookLM
      Gemini app, Google Search and Google Workspace
    
    
      Analysis capability
      Source and chat organization
      In-notebook code execution and expandable thinking steps for eligible users
    
    
      Availability direction
      Web access for AI Ultra, Pro and Plus subscribers
      Initial Ultra and Workspace AI Ultra Access rollout, then Pro access on the web
    
  



  
  
  What visible thinking steps mean


Google's support documentation says advanced users on Google AI Ultra and Pro can expand Gemini Notebook's thinking steps to view details of what the model is doing during chat and notebook operations. This is a documented interface feature, not a guarantee that every model operation will be fully explained or that the displayed steps are a complete record of all model reasoning.

That distinction matters. The feature can give users more operational context when Gemini Notebook is analyzing sources or responding to a question, but Google describes the advanced reasoning features as experimental and cautions that mistakes remain possible. Thinking steps should therefore be treated as an aid to inspection, not as proof that an output is correct.

Gemini Notebook's source-grounding design provides a separate reliability mechanism. Its responses are intended to be grounded in uploaded materials and include citations, allowing users to compare claims with the underlying sources. In practice, citations and human review remain the more direct controls for validating research outputs.


  
  
  Access, pricing and platform questions


The available information points to tiered access, rather than a single Gemini Notebook price. Google has linked different stages of access and higher limits to Google AI, Workspace and qualifying plan tiers. Ultra and Pro are specifically identified for the expandable thinking-steps capability, while Plus was included in the earlier web rollout for notebooks in Gemini.

Google has not provided a complete, flat pricing breakdown for every Gemini Notebook capability in the supplied announcements. Organizations evaluating access should distinguish between basic notebook availability, advanced feature eligibility and Workspace plan limits instead of assuming that every subscriber receives the same tools.

The rollout is also platform-dependent. Google's announcements establish web access first and describe mobile expansion as a future step. Cross-product syncing is central to the product's direction, but businesses should verify the features available to their specific account type and plan before standardizing a workflow around Gemini Notebook.


  
  
  Governance starts with sources and review


For organizations, the practical value of Gemini Notebook depends on whether the product can be used within existing data-handling and review processes. Google says uploaded sources remain private unless users share them and are not used to train models. That claim is particularly relevant for teams assessing whether proprietary research, internal documentation or client materials can be placed in a notebook.

The product's combination of citations, source-based outputs and visible thinking steps can support more reviewable AI-assisted research. It does not remove governance responsibilities. Teams still need to decide who may upload and share source material, how generated outputs are checked, and when human approval is required before analysis informs a decision.

Organizations that want to connect source-grounded AI research to existing systems can work with Scalevise on AI architecture, workflow automation and implementation, including governance-aware integration planning.


  
  
  Frequently Asked Questions


What is Gemini Notebook?

Gemini Notebook is Google's evolved NotebookLM product and a research workspace integrated with the Gemini app, Google Search and Google Workspace. It is designed to organize sources, chats and project materials.

Can users see Gemini Notebook's thinking steps?

Yes. Google's support documentation says Google AI Ultra and Pro users can expand thinking steps to see details of what Gemini Notebook is doing during chat and notebook operations.

Are Gemini Notebook thinking steps a guarantee that an answer is correct?

No. Google describes the related advanced features as experimental and warns that mistakes can occur. Users should review cited sources and apply human oversight.

Which plans have access to Gemini Notebook features?

Access is rolling out by plan and feature. Google identified AI Ultra and Workspace AI Ultra Access for the initial expanded rollout, followed by Pro users on the web. Earlier notebooks in Gemini access also included Plus subscribers on the web.

Does Google use uploaded Gemini Notebook sources to train models?

Google says uploaded sources stay private unless shared and are not used to train models.





  
  
  Conclusion


Gemini Notebook represents a broader shift from a standalone notebook tool toward a connected Google research workspace. Expandable thinking steps add useful visibility for eligible users, but the product's strongest controls remain source grounding, citations and human review. As access expands across plans and platforms, governance and plan-specific feature checks will be essential for organizations adopting it.

title: Code Review Practice in The Age of AI
title_hi: Code Review Practice in The Age of AI
summary: As AI agents can write code much faster than any human developer ever could, and as we get hundreds if not thousands lin
content:
As AI agents can write code much faster than any human developer ever could, and as we get hundreds if not thousands lines of code as a results of one prompt, the need for careful code review is greater than ever. This remains the primary mechanism for ensuring that code is following engineering guidelines, architectural principles and in the same time ensures long-term maintainability and extensibility.

In one of my previous posts about vibe coding traps and delusions I have shared my thoughts on why and how the cognitive load is shifted from the code generation to the code review and why I think this is the topic that should attract more and more attention from fellow developers. In this article, I describe how I see the approach to the code review after more than a year of actively working with coding agents.




  
  
  Active Code Review By The Author


Before requesting a peer review, the author should perform an active review of the generated code as if they were reviewing someone else’s work. Before AI, developers usually understood every line because they had actively participated in writing the code. Today, developers often guide the implementation rather than author every detail of it. With that being said, making an explicit self-review becomes much more important in order to be sure that agent generated what is intended.

This can be understood as a logical step, but as agents are writing comprehensive implementations and the syntax of the generated code appears to be very persuasive, it is not hard to believe everything what comes as an output from the agent is correct and to not pay enough attention on details. First thing that needs to be checked is if the generated code aligns with the architecture principles in the product and if the code is solving the right problem or inventing new one.

Another step is to try to do the same functionality with less code as possible. As LLMs by default are generating more code, sometimes more complex as it should be, we need to check if all that code is needed. In most cases it can be simplified, and we should insist on it as much as possible. Of course, at the beginning you will be in situation that you need to prompt back and forth till the desired output is given, but this is also the process where you can learn how to steer your agent in the way that fit your needs.

In the process, you will discover some patterns what fit your workflow, so you can define skills for the agent. In that way you already have predefined input for the agent next time you need some repetitive task. Both skills and rules can be used to streamline the code generation process. However, neither skills nor rules eliminate the need for careful code review. In the end, the author remains responsible for every line that is submitted.


  
  
  Automated Review


Once the developer is ready to open a pull request, another step is often executed automatically as part of the CI pipeline. Here, the AI agent is doing automated review on the posted code and can find some very interesting edge cases, potential security risks or missing null checks. In the same time it still lacks the full business and historical context of the project. It may recommend changes that are technically reasonable but inappropriate for the product or existing architecture.

Here, the developer again should pay full attention on the feedback from automated reviewer to check if the review makes sense and if it is worth to be implemented. Again, we can expect here lot of suggestions, depending on the size of the pull request. Large AI generated pull requests often trigger a significant number of automated review comments. This is another reason to keep changes as small and focused as possible, to be able to carefully review them.


  
  
  Code Review By Peer


If all previous steps are done correctly, then this stage should not take too much time, because much of the confidence should already come from the author’s own review and the automated review. This stage then is basically similar as the old fashioned code review before AI. Deep insights into this can be found in one of my older posts about code review so if you haven’t checked it yet, maybe now is good time to do it.

But, if some of the previous steps are poorly done, especially the first one, then the code reviewer is not in a thankful position, because entire responsibility for code quality is now shifted towards him. First problem here is that the developer who raised the pull request probably does not understand the code he authored, and this later can produce more issues when it comes to unexpected exceptions or maintenance. The author’s name is attached to the commit, but they cannot confidently explain why parts of the implementation exist or how they work.

Looking at the entire AI movement in the past years, I see one alarming thing if this is not handled correctly. It goes in the direction where teams are producing code much faster then ever before, but in the same time, senior engineers increasingly spend their time reviewing and validating AI-generated changes rather than writing new implementations themselves. In that case, AI accelerates code generation without necessarily accelerating software delivery.


  
  
  Takeaways and Conclusion


AI has definitely changed where engineering effort is spent. Writing the code is becoming increasingly automated, but understanding, validating, and maintaining that same code remain human responsibility. Teams that recognize this shift and adapt their review process accordingly can benefit far more from AI than those who focus solely on generating code faster. Over time, that code will become harder to maintain if not even impossible.

Most important lesson I have learned is to keep code amount per pull request as small as possible, because it is easier then for the developer to review it and also for the peer to take a look at it. Large pull requests help neither the author nor the reviewer. They just increase uncertainty and reduce the confidence in the delivered product.

content:
This is a submission for Frontend Challenge - Comfort Food Edition, Perfect Landing


  
  
  What I Built


I built Dosa Therapy, a colorful and playful landing page that treats dosa less like a meal and more like an emotional support system.

The idea came from how deeply comfort food is tied to mood. A crispy dosa, hot sambar, fresh chutney, and filter coffee can genuinely make a bad day feel slightly more manageable. So instead of creating a conventional restaurant landing page, I imagined a fictional therapy experience centered entirely around dosa.

The page takes users through the different layers of the dosa experience, from the batter and rice varieties to sambar, chutneys, dosa personalities, and mood-based recommendations.

Visually, I wanted the site to feel energetic, warm, and slightly chaotic in the best way. I avoided food photography and built the experience using bold geometric illustrations, expressive typography, vibrant colors, and playful animations.


  
  
  Demo




🥞 Live Demo:
https://dosatherapy.vercel.app

💻 Source Code:
https://github.com/krxthx/dosa-therapy


  
  
  Journey


I began with a much simpler idea: a bright landing page about dosa. But while exploring the concept, I realized that simply presenting dosa varieties and ingredients felt too similar to a restaurant menu.

That led to the idea of Dosa Therapy, a playful wellness-inspired brand where every mood has a corresponding dosa prescription.

One of the most important creative decisions was to use a fully illustrated visual style rather than realistic food images. I wanted the site to feel like its own tiny universe, with geometric dosas, animated chutney bowls, expressive ingredients, and sections that feel different while still belonging to the same visual system.

I particularly enjoyed building the sections around:


The anatomy of a comforting dosa meal
Different rice varieties used in dosa batter
Sambar and chutney as essential supporting characters
Popular dosa variants with their own personalities
Mood-based dosa recommendations
A filter coffee-inspired ending to complete the experience


The most challenging part was balancing all the colors, illustrations, typography, and movement without making the page feel visually overwhelming. I spent a lot of time adjusting spacing, section transitions, responsive layouts, and animation timing so the experience would still feel intentional.

I am especially proud that the final result does not look like a generic food landing page. It feels playful, culturally familiar, and very specifically about the joy of eating dosa.

Given more time, I would love to add a more interactive “Find Your Dosa” experience, richer scroll-based animations, and additional regional dosa varieties.

Because sometimes the solution is not deep breathing.

Sometimes it is dosa. <3

title: Empower your agents with the new SurrealDB MCP
title_hi: Empower your agents with the new SurrealDB MCP
summary: Exactly a year ago we released SurrealMCP, a server you had to install and run in order to connect agents to your Surrea
content:
Exactly a year ago we released SurrealMCP, a server you had to install and run in order to connect agents to your SurrealDB instance. Today, we're excited to announce the next evolution in agent intelligence with the new hosted SurrealDB MCP server.

With this new SurrealDB MCP server, all you need is to add one URL to your AI tool of choice, sign in with your SurrealDB account, and your assistant can work on your instances or contexts alongside you. Whether you want to deploy a new instance, spin up a new Spectron context, execute queries against your graph, or ask questions about your data, the new SurrealDB MCP server has you covered.

Let's dive into it! 🎉


  
  
  Getting started



  
  
  Adding the SurrealDB MCP to your agent




Previously, you would need to add an MCP configuration for every instance or context that you wanted to connect to, and there was no way to provision instances or contexts with an agent. With the new hosted SurrealDB MCP server, you can do all of this and much more by adding a single URL:



https://mcp.surrealdb.com






You can authorise the SurrealDB MCP Server either through signing in to your SurrealDB account, or for fine grained control, create a personal access token from the account portal. That is the whole setup. Once connected, your agent now has the ability to interact with your SurrealDB Cloud resources.

Looking to setup your agent? We have step-by-step guides for setting up with Claude and Cursor.  For other configurations, please see our MCP docs. 


  
  
  Deploy and manage resources just by asking




Everything you would normally click through in the SurrealDB Studio dashboard is available in your conversations. Deploy a new instance or context, expand your resources as you grow, or upgrade to the latest version of SurrealDB. When deploying resources, the MCP server can put together a configuration, give you a cost estimation, and wait for your confirmation to kick off.

The same conversation can also cover the rest of the housekeeping such as inviting users to your organisation, managing their access level, checking your monthly spend, and updating your instances.


  
  
  Ask questions about your data and build with ease





Note
Instance querying is only available on instances running SurrealDB 3.2.3 and above


The usual way to get an AI assistant to look at your database is to copy a schema or a query into a chat window, then paste the results back out again. SurrealDB MCP removes this loop. Simply ask a question in plain language and your assistant finds the right database, writes the query, runs it, and shows you both the query it wrote and what came back.

You don't have to describe the shape of your data first, because it can go and look. Ask how many orders you took last week grouped by status, and it will find the table, work out the fields, and write the aggregate itself. Ask what the customer table actually says, and it will describe the fields and indexes back to you. As a bonus, it's often faster than opening SurrealDB Studio to check for yourself.

It works the other way round too. While you're building something new, you can ask it to create a single table or an entire schema for an enterprise-level app.


  
  
  Memory that outlasts the conversation




Every new chat normally starts from nothing. A decision your team made three weeks ago is gone unless someone remembers to paste it back in. My favorite feature of SurrealDB MCP is that you can interact directly with Spectron, our memory layer for AI agents, in order to keep a persistent brain related to your chats which can be shared with multiple users. 

Simply ask your agent to save a memory or give it documents to read, and it will search through them by meaning rather than by keyword and store it for you. Then, ask your agent to retrieve something later:




  
  
  Let us know what you think


We'd love to hear your thoughts! Join us on Discord to ask questions, share what you're building, or tell us what you'd like your assistant to be able to do next.

To learn even more about SurrealDB MCP, please check out our MCP docs.

title: Building an AI Startup? Solve Business Problems Before Writing Code

content:
Every week, a new AI tool launches with the promise of transforming an industry.

Yet, despite rapid advances in large language models, automation frameworks, and AI agents, many AI startups struggle to gain traction.

Why?

Because customers don't buy AI—they buy solutions to problems.


  
  
  Technology Is No Longer the Biggest Barrier


Building AI applications has become easier than ever.

Open-source models, cloud APIs, and low-code platforms allow developers to create prototypes in days instead of months.

The real challenge has shifted from "Can we build it?" to "Will anyone actually use it?"

That question should guide every product decision.


  
  
  Find an Expensive Problem


The best AI companies solve expensive problems for corporations.

These may be:


Automation of repetitive admin work
Speeding up customer support response times
Data mining insights from big data
Processing documents better
Improving workflows within businesses
Supporting decision making


If the problem being solved produces value, then companies will be far more interested in the solution.


  
  
  Validate Before Scaling


It is easy to spend months perfecting prompts, increasing accuracy, and developing advanced features.

But validate the idea first.

Speak to the potential customers.

Figure out how they currently solve the problem.

Discover what makes them angry.

Then design the smallest solution possible which demonstrates your core value proposition.


  
  
  User Experience is Key


The best AI models are useless if they confuse users.

The most successful AI solutions focus on:


Easy-to-use interfaces
Quick responses
Reliable results
Clarity in explanation
Easier onboarding


The tool should make things easier, not harder.


  
  
  Impact Metrics for Your Business


Forget about measuring your model’s success rate; measure what really matters to your customers:


Time savings
Cost savings
Increases in productivity
Satisfaction of customers
Retention rates
ROI


This is what makes sense to businesses when they evaluate your AI solution.


  
  
  AI Is Part of the Solution


Customers don’t typically request AI.

Customers want their processes to be quicker and more effective and cost-efficient.

And this is where AI can help.

Having such an approach will allow founders to develop a product relevant regardless of technological changes in the future.


  
  
  Final Words


The future of success for AI companies will not be about having the most advanced models out there.

It will be about their ability to solve problems for businesses effectively.

Before coding a thousand lines of AI, ask yourself one thing:

Is this problem going to remain relevant without AI in the picture?

And if it is, it’s safe to say that your product will have some real potential to it.

title: OpenAI o3 Model Explained: The Next Frontier in AI Reasoning

The OpenAI o3 model is a reasoning-focused AI model designed to handle complex questions that require logic, analysis, planning, coding, mathematics, and multi-step decision-making. Instead of relying only on pattern recognition, it is optimized to evaluate information more carefully before generating a response.

This makes it particularly useful for tasks where accuracy and structured thinking are more important than simply producing fluent text.

Earlier AI models became extremely good at conversation, writing, and summarization. However, they sometimes struggled with:

Multi-step reasoning
Complex mathematics
Programming logic
Scientific analysis
Long-term planning
Decision making
The o3 model addresses these challenges by improving its reasoning capabilities, enabling it to solve more difficult problems with greater consistency.

Advanced Reasoning
The biggest strength of o3 is its ability to reason through problems step by step. This allows it to perform better on tasks that require logical thinking rather than simple text prediction.

Improved Coding Assistance

Debug code
Explain algorithms
Generate software solutions
Optimize existing programs
Review code quality
Build automation scripts
Its reasoning abilities make it especially useful for software engineering workflows.

Better Mathematical Performance
The model performs well on:

Algebra
Calculus
Statistics
Probability
Financial calculations
Data analysis
Instead of relying on memorized answers, it works through mathematical problems more effectively.

Stronger Scientific Understanding

Scientific explanations
Research summaries
Data interpretation
Experimental design
Literature reviews
The reasoning improvements help produce more structured and coherent analyses.

Long Context Processing
The model can understand large documents, making it useful for:

Legal contracts
Research papers
Technical documentation
Business reports
Academic articles
This enables users to ask detailed questions about lengthy content.

How Does OpenAI o3 Differ From Earlier Models?
Compared to previous generations, o3 places greater emphasis on reasoning quality.

Some notable improvements include:

More reliable answers
Better planning
Stronger logical consistency
Improved code generation
More accurate mathematical reasoning
Enhanced document understanding
Better instruction following
Rather than focusing only on speed, it prioritizes thoughtful and well-structured responses.

Real-World Applications
The OpenAI o3 model can be used across many industries.

Software Development
Developers use it for:

Code generation
Debugging
API development
Documentation
Refactoring
Education
Students and educators benefit from:

Personalized tutoring
Homework assistance
Concept explanations
Exam preparation
Research support
Business
Companies can use o3 for:

Strategic planning
Market analysis
Customer support
Report generation
Workflow automation
Healthcare
Potential applications include:

Medical documentation
Clinical research support
Healthcare administration
Knowledge management
AI should assist professionals rather than replace expert medical judgment.

Finance
Financial professionals can use reasoning models for:

Risk analysis
Financial forecasting
Investment research
Spreadsheet automation
Report preparation
Benefits of OpenAI o3
Organizations adopting reasoning-focused AI can experience several advantages:

Higher accuracy on complex tasks
Better problem-solving
Improved productivity

More reliable automation
Better research assistance

These benefits make reasoning models valuable across technical and professional domains.

For legal, financial, or medical matters, expert review remains essential.

Best Practices for Using OpenAI o3
To get the best results:

Write clear prompts.
Provide relevant context.
Break large tasks into smaller steps.
Verify important information.
Ask follow-up questions for clarification.
Use structured prompts for complex projects.
Good prompting often leads to significantly better outputs.

The Future of AI Reasoning

Stronger scientific reasoning
Improved autonomous workflows
More reliable coding assistance
Enhanced multimodal understanding
Greater collaboration between humans and AI

Final Thoughts
The OpenAI o3 model marks an important milestone in the evolution of artificial intelligence. By emphasizing reasoning, logic, and structured problem-solving, it goes beyond traditional text generation to tackle complex real-world challenges more effectively. Whether you're a developer, researcher, student, or business professional, o3 can help streamline workflows, improve decision-making, and enhance productivity.

title: Web Development Best Practices in 2026: Building Websites That Grow With Your Business

content:
A business website is no longer just a place to display products or services. Today, it supports marketing, customer engagement, lead generation, and sometimes even core business operations.

As expectations continue to grow, building a successful website requires more than an attractive design. Performance, scalability, security, and user experience have become essential parts of modern web development.

Whether you're launching a new project or improving an existing platform, focusing on the right fundamentals can help create a website that delivers value for years to come.

Think Beyond the Launch

Many businesses see a website launch as the finish line. In reality, it's only the beginning.

Customer expectations change, businesses introduce new services, and technology continues to evolve. A website should be built with future updates in mind so new features and improvements can be added without major redevelopment.

Planning for long-term growth helps reduce maintenance costs and keeps the platform adaptable.

Performance Creates Better User Experiences

Visitors expect websites to load almost instantly. If pages are slow, many users leave before exploring the content.

Good performance comes from smart development decisions, including:

Optimized images and media
Efficient code structure
Reduced unnecessary scripts
Reliable hosting
Fast server response times

A faster website improves usability and helps businesses build trust with their audience.

User Experience Should Guide Every Decision

Good design is about more than visual appearance.

Visitors should be able to understand what your business offers, navigate easily, and complete important actions without confusion.

Simple navigation, clear content, and logical page structures often have a greater impact than complex animations or visual effects.

The easier a website is to use, the more likely visitors are to stay engaged.

Build Mobile-First

A significant share of website traffic now comes from mobile devices.

Designing with mobile users in mind ensures pages remain readable, navigation stays simple, and important actions are easy to complete on smaller screens.

A consistent experience across desktop, tablet, and mobile devices has become a basic expectation rather than an optional feature.
**
Never Ignore Security**

Modern websites handle valuable business and customer information.

Security should be part of the development process from day one through:

Secure authentication
Data protection
Regular software updates
Strong access controls
Ongoing maintenance

Protecting user information helps build trust and reduces potential risks.

Websites Should Continue to Evolve

Successful websites aren't finished after deployment.

Monitoring performance, collecting user feedback, updating content, and improving functionality help businesses stay competitive as customer needs change.

Treating a website as an evolving product instead of a one-time project often leads to better long-term results.

Final Thoughts

Modern web development is about creating digital experiences that support business goals, not simply publishing information online.

A well-built website combines speed, security, scalability, and a great user experience to create lasting value for both businesses and their customers.

Under the hood it is one always-on gateway on my machine: a scheduler for the standing jobs, persistent memory that survives every restart, subagents for parallel work, and a lessons system that saves every correction I make so it never repeats a mistake. That last part matters more than any of it.

What surprised me was not the speed but the scope. The launch post from the three engineers who built it describes what happened inside Amazon: a side project became "something maintained by a community across many roles, not just engineers." In under six months it reached more than 39,000 builders, with nearly 500 contributors shipping 597 updates. I am one of those roles. I now prototype features, review architecture, and make one change land everywhere it needs to, from task boards to monthly reviews to launch announcements. Work that used to sit outside my role, or spread across five tools, now completes end to end.

Here is the honest part. The unlock was never the technology. It was making my own decision-making explicit enough to delegate. The months I spent teaching this system my rules, what good writing looks like, which data sources to trust, when to interrupt me, are the reason it performs.

Here is what that looks like. The agent built me a chart of adoption by role. Every number in it was correct. The chart was still wrong. One row was a worldwide rate and another was a single country, sitting in the same column, which made one team look like the worst performer when it wasn't. Nothing in the data flagged that. The rule was in my head, not the spreadsheet. So I wrote it down: one population per column, label the scope, exceptions get their own chart. It has not made that mistake since. That is the shift. I spend less time producing the analysis and more time writing down the standard the analysis has to meet.

The code is open source now. The judgment you encode in it will be yours.

Along the way I used it deeply enough to contribute to its Slack integration. My first code contribution to a platform I use every day.

Kiro Crew is out now. Whether you build software every day or have never opened a terminal, it meets you where you are. Start with one decision you make every week. Teach it that. Let it take the job from there.

title: Graph Engineering: The Missing Skill Behind Modern AI Agents
title_hi: आधुनिक एआई एजेंटों के पीछे छिपी कौशल: ग्राफ इंजीनियरिंग
summary: Discover Graph Engineering for modern AI agents
content: Everyone is talking about AI agents, but many developers still build them as simple linear pipelines. Graph Engineering is the practice of designing AI workflows as interconnected nodes rather than a single chain of prompts. This makes AI systems more flexible, maintainable, and reliable. Traditional pipelines have limitations, such as being difficult to debug and having limited branching. Graph-based workflows solve these problems by allowing conditional routing, parallel execution, and retry logic.
content_hi: एआई एजेंटों की चर्चा सभी में है, लेकिन कई डेवलपर्स अभी भी उन्हें सरल रेखीय पाइपलाइन के रूप में बनाते हैं। ग्राफ इंजीनियरिंग एआई वर्कफ्लो को एकल प्रॉम्प्ट श्रृंखला के बजाय इंटरकनेक्टेड नोड्स के रूप में डिज़ाइन करने का अभ्यास है। यह एआई सिस्टम को अधिक लचीला, रखरखाव योग्य और विश्वसनीय बनाता है।

title: Stop Chasing Perfect Prompts, Design Systems Instead

summary: Optimize AI workflows with prompt systems
content: Developers often focus on optimization, which led to a surge in optimizing ChatGPT prompts. However, a prompt is essentially a function, and a prompt system is an application.
